title: 7. Why the Price Is What It Is: Valuation, Reverse DCF & Peer Comps

epigraph.quote: Price is what you pay; value is what you get. When a cyclical manufacturer trades at software-like multiples, you are paying upfront for factories not yet built.
epigraph.author: Institutional Underwriting Maxim

web_blocks.html: On 13 November 2026, Tanfac Industries Ltd. (BSE: TANFACIND) closed at ₹3,349.40 per share [32]. Its market cap reached ₹7,245.95 Cr (₹7,246 Cr on Screener) on the post-QIP equity base [6, 32]. The stock sits 8.19% below its ₹3,648.00 52-week high and 105.2% above its ₹1,632.60 low, up +72.38% YoY [32]. Yet the valuation paradox is stark. Tanfac trades at 99.32x TTM P/E on TradingView (104x on Screener) and 9.83x P/B [6, 32]. At the same time, TTM EPS contracted 28.49% YoY, and Q2 FY27 OPM compressed to 11.84% [8, 32].

Investors at ₹3,349.40 are not valuing FY26's ₹70.14 Cr PAT or Q2 FY27's ₹19.03 Cr PAT [8, 20]. Instead, the market is pricing in two future growth engines. First, Tanfac raised ₹349.41 Cr in 2026—₹250 Cr via QIP at ₹1,965.83/sh and ₹99.41 Cr via preferential allotment [17, 19]. That equity funds a ₹495 Cr, 20,000 TPA HFC-32 refrigerant plant [11, 17]. Second, buyers are capitalizing the ₹732 Cr Kredence Solar-Grade DHF contract through FY29 [9, 14].

web_blocks.takeaway: At ₹3,349.40, TANFACIND trades at a 70.4% premium to its June 2026 QIP price and ~100x trailing earnings despite a -28.49% YoY TTM EPS contraction.

web_blocks.html: A Reverse DCF reveals the exact math embedded in ₹3,349.40. Assume a 12.0% WACC, 5.0% terminal growth, and 25%–30% reinvestment. To justify a ~₹7,150 Cr enterprise value, Tanfac must compound FCFF at 24%–26% annually for ten years. Revenue must scale 4x from ₹711 Cr (FY26) to ₹2,800–3,200 Cr by FY32–FY33 [20]. EBITDA margins must also rebound from Q2 FY27's 11.84% to a sustained 20%–22% [6, 8].

web_blocks.title: Reverse DCF Reality Check: Zero Margin of Safety
paragraphs: At 99.32x TTM P/E, the market is paying upfront for three simultaneous wins: (1) full ramp-up of the ₹732 Cr Kredence Solar-Grade DHF contract without pricing givebacks, (2) on-time, on-budget commissioning of the ₹495 Cr HFC-32 plant with healthy refrigerant spreads, and (3) an 800–1,000 bps EBITDA margin recovery from Q2 FY27's 11.84% trough. If any one of those three legs stumbles—or if Chinese R-32/HF imports cap spreads—the multiple has room to compress from 100x toward 45x–55x.

web_blocks.takeaway: TANFACIND commands the highest trailing P/E (104x Screener / 99.3x TV) in the Indian fluorochemical peer group—nearly double Navin Fluorine (56.4x) and over triple SRF (32.1x)—despite single-site concentration and 11.84% Q2 FY27 OPM.

web_blocks.html: Peer multiples sharpen this critique [36]. Navin Fluorine (NAVINFLUOR) carries a ₹51,462.90 Cr market cap and 22.6% ROE. Yet it trades at just 56.4x P/E [36]. SRF Limited (SRF), India's refrigerant leader (₹72,621.86 Cr market cap), trades at 32.1x P/E [36]. Even Gujarat Fluorochemicals (FLUOROCHEM) trades at 76.2x P/E [36]. Tanfac's 99.3x–104x P/E is nearly double Navin Fluorine's multiple despite single-site Cuddalore risk.

What Would Change Our Valuation View: Either a correction into the ₹2,100–₹2,400 range (closer to the ₹1,965.83 QIP price) or two quarters of verified OPM recovery above 18% with >75% CFO/EBITDA conversion.

book_paragraphs: Now let us unlock the market ledger and ask the single hardest question in investing: at ₹3,349.40 per share on 13 November 2026, what is the stock market already assuming about Tanfac Industries? Remember what we proved in Pass 1 before we ever looked at a price quote. Tanfac is a genuinely upgraded business—Anupam Rasayan and TIDCO have doubled AHF capacity, commissioned India's only Solar-Grade DHF line backed by a ₹732 Cr Kredence contract, and raised ₹349.41 Cr in fresh equity to build a ₹495 Cr HFC-32 plant. Yet we also stamped it CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL because Q2 FY27 operating margins just compressed to 11.84%, FY26 cash conversion lagged at 56% of EBITDA, and 100% of operations sit on one Cuddalore site.

When you put that business reality next to a ₹7,245.95 Cr market capitalization, the numbers jolt you awake. At ₹3,349.40, Tanfac trades at 99.32 times trailing earnings on TradingView—104 times on Screener—and 9.83 times post-raise book value. Think about that for a moment. In June 2026, institutional buyers in the ₹250 Cr QIP subscribed at ₹1,965.83 per share. Five months later, the market is asking you and me to pay ₹3,349.40—a 70.4% markup over the QIP price—even though trailing twelve-month EPS fell 28.49% year-on-year.

Let us run the Reverse DCF together so we do not guess. At a ₹7,100 to ₹7,200 Cr enterprise value, assuming a 12% cost of capital and a 5% terminal growth rate, the market is pricing in roughly 24% to 26% annual free cash flow compounding for the next ten years. For a chemical plant, that means revenue must quadruple from ₹711 Cr toward ₹3,000 Cr by FY32–FY33 while operating margins snap back from 11.84% to 20%–22% and stay there. In other words, ₹3,349.40 pays upfront for both the Solar-Grade DHF ramp and a flawless HFC-32 launch at peak-cycle spreads.

Compare that against India's established fluorochemical leaders. Navin Fluorine commands a ₹51,325 Cr market cap with multi-site CDMO capabilities and a 21.0% ROCE, yet trades at 56.0x P/E. SRF, the heavyweight in refrigerants including HFC-32, trades at 31.1x P/E. Paying nearly 100x earnings for Tanfac means you are paying almost double Navin Fluorine's multiple and triple SRF's multiple for a single-site company whose quarterly margin just printed 11.84%. That does not make Tanfac a bad company; it makes the current stock price unforgiving.

To make our Reverse DCF in Chapter 7 concrete, think about what a ₹7,246 crore market cap demands in rupees and paise. In FY26, Tanfac earned ₹70.14 crore of net profit on ₹711.07 crore of sales. Even if Tanfac grows revenue at 22% every single year for seven years—reaching roughly ₹2,850 crore by FY33—and expands net margins from 9.9% back to 13% (requiring ~20% EBITDA margins), FY33 net profit would be around ₹370 crore. Discounting that future cash stream back to today at a 12% cost of capital leaves almost no upside buffer above ₹3,349.40.

That is why the peer comparison with Navin Fluorine and SRF is so sobering. Both Navin Fluorine (56.0x P/E) and SRF (31.1x P/E) operate multi-site chemical complexes across Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, and Rajasthan, reducing single-plant shutdown risk, and both possess deep R&D pipelines in complex fluorination. Tanfac trades at nearly double Navin Fluorine's multiple despite single-site Cuddalore exposure and a 11.84% Q2 FY27 operating margin.

Ask yourself a simple sanity-check question about Reverse DCF: how many Indian chemical companies with ₹711 crore of annual revenue have successfully quadrupled sales to ₹3,000 crore over seven years while simultaneously expanding EBITDA margins from 12% to 21% without a single cyclical setback? A handful of exceptional CDMO platforms achieved it, and almost none did it from a single manufacturing site.

Even if Tanfac executes well and reaches ₹1,000 crore of revenue in FY28 at a 16% EBITDA margin, net profit would likely land around ₹90 to ₹95 crore—meaning at today's ₹7,246 crore market cap, you are still paying roughly 76 to 80 times FY28 earnings two years in advance. Paying 80x two-year-forward earnings for a cyclical chemical producer leaves zero room for error.

Step back and look at the valuation gap in plain rupee terms. At ₹3,349.40 per share, Tanfac is valued at ₹7,246 crore—roughly 10.2 times its entire FY26 revenue and 99.3 times its trailing net profit. Even if you give management full credit for executing the ₹732 crore Kredence contract and commissioning HFC-32 by FY28–FY29, you are paying today's market price as though both factories are already running at peak 20% margins with zero Chinese competition. That leaves no margin of safety for an investor deploying fresh capital.

Think about the asymmetry of expectations at ₹3,349.40. When a stock trades at 99.32x trailing earnings and 9.83x book value, good news is already in the price—an inline quarter with 12% margins merely holds the stock flat, while any delay in Kredence DHF offtake or HFC-32 permitting risks a sharp de-rating toward 50x–60x earnings. Conversely, at ₹2,100–₹2,300, the same industrial franchise would offer genuine upside optionality.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: When a stock rallies 70% above its institutional QIP price in five months while quarterly operating margins compress from 28% to 11.84%, the market is no longer pricing current earnings—it is discounting 2029 factory perfection.
